keyVerseText: And shall lay thee even with the ground, and thy children within thee; and they shall not leave in thee one stone upon another; because thou knewest not the time of thy visitation.
rootMeaning: The word ἐπισκοπή (episkopḗ) derives from the verb ἐπισκέπτομαι (episképtomai), which means to look out, visit, or inspect. This root sense conveys an active watching over or careful examination, often with the intent to provide relief or care. Unlike the English glosses that focus on formal titles or offices, the root meaning emphasizes the personal, attentive aspect of oversight and visitation.
usageInScripture: In Scripture, ἐπισκοπή appears only four times and is translated variously as visitation, bishoprick, the office of a bishop, and of visitation. This range shows the word’s flexibility, encompassing both the concrete act of visiting—sometimes divine visitation—and the formal responsibility or charge associated with church leadership. The consistency lies in the idea of oversight or inspection, whether by God or by human leaders.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding ἐπισκοπή in its original sense enriches our grasp of biblical leadership and divine action. The term points to a ministry that is not merely administrative but involves vigilant care and spiritual oversight, reflecting God’s own way of visiting His people in mercy or judgment. This highlights the sacred responsibility entrusted to church overseers to watch over the flock as God watches over His covenant community. Recognizing the word’s root meaning encourages believers to see episcopal authority as a calling to active, loving supervision modeled on God’s visitation.
keyVerseReflection: Luke 19:44 warns that the city will be leveled because its inhabitants did not recognize the time of their visitation. Here, ἐπισκοπή underscores God’s sovereign act of coming near—whether in mercy or judgment—as a moment requiring awareness and response. The word’s connotation of careful inspection and oversight deepens the urgency of the warning: missing God’s visitation means failing to heed His watchful care and timely intervention.
